co_sunshine_buttress_aka_wichita_wall.blurb: A south-facing gneiss wall in 10 Mile Canyon, high in the mountains near Frisco beside the interstate. Roughly eighteen climbs, nearly all of them trad on slabs, faces and roofs, with a few bolted lines and a single boulder problem. Grades start around 5.6 and run to 5.11, with the largest cluster at 5.10 and under, so it suits confident moderate leaders. The wall is divided into west, central and east sections. Falls onto the ledges and slabs can be long, so it is a poor choice for a casual family outing. Strong sun makes it a late-spring to fall crag, and the talus below turns slick when damp.

co_finger_flatiron.blurb: A slim, tall flatiron in the Central Flatirons above Boulder, standing just north of the Hand and Mallory Cave. The conglomerate here holds eighteen climbs spread across trad, sport and top-rope. Difficulty ranges from an easy 5.4 on the east face up to the low 5.12s on a short bolted line, but the bulk of the routes sit at 5.11, so it leans toward strong climbers. Moderate trad is available on the longer lines, and a short rappel off the summit gets you down. Expect a steady walk in from the Mallory Cave trail, and plan around summer afternoon storms.

co_krishna_west.blurb: A broad cliff in Lower Dream Canyon, off Boulder Canyon west of Boulder, sitting beside Krishna Spire. It is around 300 feet across and very tall, with steep crack systems below and looser, ledgier ground higher up. Most routes are single pitches of 70 to 125 feet. The roughly eighteen climbs are mainly trad with a handful of bolted lines, running from 5.9 up to 5.12, and most fall between 5.9 and 5.11. A creek-side walk and a steep gully lead to the base, which makes this a destination for solid crack climbers rather than beginners.

co_goat_rock.blurb: A south-facing sport crag beside US 40 a few miles from Empire, at roughly 9,000 feet. Almost every climb is bolted, with a lone trad line, and there are about thirteen independent lines including some two-pitch routes. The range runs from 5.8 into the low 5.13s, but the weight is firmly on 5.11 and 5.12, so it rewards hard sport climbers. Rock quality is mixed: parts are loose, while the newer lines higher up follow cleaner granite. A quick talus path leads to the base. Despite the altitude, south exposure keeps the season longer than you would guess, with climbing possible well into December.

co_trail_boulders.blurb: A cluster of roughly eighteen boulder problems on the east side of the Arkansas River in Buena Vista, strung along riverside trails right at the edge of town. The problems begin around V2 and climb to V9, with most in the V2 to V5 window and a few hard lines for strong boulderers. Easy walking and quick access make it a good drop-in session between other activities, and the setting beside the river draws hikers and rafters too. A smaller set of River Boulders lies close by.
co_trail_boulders.parking_note: Leave the car at the river park in Buena Vista. The Trail Boulders are reached by crossing the footbridge and following the trail system on the east bank.

_expect.name: South Ridgeline, including Cat's Eye Face & Bolt Wall

co_south_ridgeline_including_cat_s_eye_f.blurb: The southern end of the ridge at Rotary Park, on the hillside above Horsetooth Reservoir near Fort Collins. Seventeen boulder problems plus one top-rope line gather around the Cat's Eye Face at the end of the path, with the Bolt Wall beside it and a slab a little further along. Difficulty is wide: easy slabs and low-grade problems up through some V7 to V10 test pieces, with a couple of highballs mixed in. It belongs to a well-loved local bouldering ridge with a long tradition, and the ridge becomes broken further north.
